title: Asking for Directions
paragraphs: Omar is visiting a new city for a business trip and looking for the nearest mosque before Dhuhr prayer. He does not know this area well, so he decides to ask someone before he wastes too much time walking around.

He sees a shopkeeper arranging bread near a small stall. "Excuse me, where is the mosque?" Omar asks politely. "It is near the market. Turn left, then walk straight for about five minutes," the shopkeeper explains carefully.

"Thank you very much for your help," Omar replies with genuine gratitude. He follows the simple directions, checking the street signs along the way. A few minutes later, he finds the mosque, just in time before the prayer begins.

After the prayer, Omar reflects that asking a stranger for help, though it felt slightly awkward at first, saved him a lot of stress. In an unfamiliar city, a short question can solve a problem instantly.
